reason: The hypothesis relies on the general premise that SiC can reinforce HEAs, which is mentioned as a topic in E2 but without specific results or mechanisms for the cited system. E1 concerns HEA-reinforced composites, not SiC reinforcement, and is misrepresented. No evidence supports the critical premise that caloric response is maintained, nor that SiC reduces cracking via grain boundary pinning in this alloy class.
premises: SiC particles can act as reinforcement in a high-entropy alloy matrix, improving mechanical properties.
SiC particles can reduce cracking tendency by pinning grain boundaries and reducing stress concentrations.
The addition of SiC particles will not degrade the large caloric response of the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy.
The cited evidence on SiC reinforcement in CoCrFeNi (E2) is directly transferable to the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 system.
